summary: Feed s111_double is degraded: 9.0% duplicates (301/3331) and severe SIEM overload with 4.62 Gbps bursts on 1 Gbps port (462% capacity, 3 intervals). No packet drops, VLAN, one-way or encryption issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the same packets twice (9.0% duplicates) - typical when aggregating multiple SPAN/TAP feeds covering the same traffic without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes license/storage and processing on duplicate events, inflates counts, skews correlation and detection logic, and can mask true event rates.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short window before delivery to SIEM, eliminating 9% waste without losing unique events.

findings.root_cause: Burst traffic peaks at 4.62 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps SIEM port capacity (462% overload, 3 overloaded intervals) - feed not load-balanced or filtered for tool capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM ingress port is oversubscribed and will drop packets during bursts, causing missed events, incomplete flows, and blind spots for detection despite no broker drops yet.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across a SIEM receiver cluster or add capacity via load-balancing on 5-tuple hash to keep per-port rate <80% of 1 Gbps and prevent tool-side drops; SIEM tolerates filtering/slicing if scaling not possible.
